bullets.title: NVDA CEO Resignation/Probe Dominates AI Tape — $500B Market Cap Erased
bullets.body: Jensen Huang resigned as NVDA CEO (effective immediately) following reports of an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, triggering a DOJ antitrust probe and congressional investigations into chip exports to China via Megaspeed. NVDA fell 13-17% on the week, losing ~$500B market cap. CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO; successor search underway with Ian Buck as top internal candidate. Multiple sell-side downgrades (HSBC to Hold/$170, Melius $315→$185, Evercore $465→$186, Oppenheimer to Perform, KeyBanc to Sector Weight, Baird to Neutral/$200, Craig-Hallum to Hold) while bulls (Wolfe, JPM) argue 10x CY27 EPS is a floor and 2-3 year product roadmap is intact. Retail bought $1.6B NVDA on Thursday — 10x the next-most-bought name.

bullets.title: Hawkish Fed Repricing: 3-4 Hikes Now Priced Through 2027 After Hot CPI/PPI
bullets.body: October core CPI printed +0.30% m/m for the third consecutive month (3-month annualized 3.7%); headline PPI at 6.5% y/y cycle high. Markets repriced from ~1.5 hikes to ~3-4 hikes through end-2027; Fed Funds terminal rate now seen at 4.5-4.75%. Governor Waller signaled openness to 50bp in December if inflation remains warm. 10-year yields hit 5.15%, 2-year worst week since 2024. Core PCE tracking 0.29-0.35% for October. Goldman, BofA, JPM all added a March 2027 hike to forecasts.

bullets.title: S&P 500 +0.2% on Week; Breadth Weak Despite Monday's Historic 2.3% Rally
bullets.body: S&P 500 finished +0.2% w/w (+10.5% YTD) while NDX lagged heavily. Monday saw the strongest single session since March (+2.3%) on AI de-risking and Iran de-escalation, but the week ended with technical deterioration: QQQ broke below 200-day MA, NVDA entered a $150-$200 trading range, and 63% of stocks remain in weekly downtrends. Russell 1000 Value outperformed Growth by 32% YTM — widest swing since dot-com bubble — with Value now at 97th percentile valuation (18.8x 2FY P/E).

bullets.title: AI Capex Intact but 2028 Projects Shift to 2029; Hyperscalers Preferred Over High-Beta AI
bullets.body: Multiple banks (MS, JPM, PSC) concluded post-midterm that the AI capex cycle is elongating not derailing: ~20% of US data center projects (5GW) shift from 2028 to 2029, while 2027 builds are insulated as already funded. Hyperscaler capex forecasts unchanged at $1.6T/1.8T in 2027/2028. Consensus shifted to prefer hyperscalers (AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT) over high-beta AI picks-and-shovels; powered shell providers with signed IG tenants favored over speculative neoclouds. Powered data center shortfall exceeds 30% through 2028.

bullets.title: Semis Positioning Washout — HF Net Exposure to Semis at Lowest Since Sept 2025
bullets.body: Hedge fund net flows in US Semis fell below -3z for second consecutive week; sixth straight week of selling (longest streak on record). Global HF net exposure to Semis down 67% from YTD highs; long/short ratio fell from 4.4x to 2.1x. SOX +8% YTD but sentiment is most bearish in some time. Combined 6-month positioning + price z-score at -3z, similar to late-July momentum reset. Evercore's semi cycle analysis warns P/E could compress further: MU fell to 3.6x from 18x, SNDK to 3.3x from 24x, NVDA to 11x from 67x this cycle, with NVDA target assuming 8x P/E at cycle trough.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO (ANT) Priced at $70-78/Share, $61B Raise, $1.4-1.5T Valuation
bullets.body: Anthropic filed amended S-1 with 825M shares at $70-78 (97% primary); $26B concurrent private placement from AMD, AVGO, GOOGL, MU, MSFT, NVDA, TSMC. Expected pricing Nov 18 post-close, trading Nov 19. Deal is ~6x oversubscribed; $10-15B index-tracking demand expected in first four weeks post-listing. Annualized revenue run-rate $81B as of Oct 31. Key debates: 2027 revenue target of $130B requires $40B+ quarterly run rate, viewed as aggressive; founder share class holds 50.1% voting control.

bullets.title: CRWV Beats, Addresses Financing Bear Cases — AI Infrastructure Trade Rebounds
bullets.body: CoreWeave Q3 revenue $3.66B (+168% y/y, 3% beat); non-GAAP operating margin 10% ahead of plan; Q4 guided to ~16% margins. Demand 10x available capacity through end of 2027. Pricing increased ~35% across SKUs; new 4-5yr contracts at $20-25M/MW, short-duration >$40M/MW. Company expects <$5B parent-level equity raises needed through 2027; no unsecured debt planned. Customer prepayments of $9B expected over next 3 months. CRWV +25% post-earnings; AMD/AVGO each +18-19% w/w as beneficiaries of NVDA turmoil.

bullets.title: CSCO Big Beat/Raise on AI Networking — FY27 AI Revenue Target Raised to $9B
bullets.body: Cisco Q1 revenue $18.52B beat by 2.2%; EPS $1.40 beat by 5.3%. FY27 AI infrastructure revenue raised to $9B from $7.5B — more than double FY26, expected to be 12% of total revenue. FY27 revenue guidance raised to $74.8-75.8B; FY27 EPS $5.47-5.53. Product orders +21% y/y (+47% hyperscale/cloud); firewall orders +30%+ for third consecutive quarter. Gross margin headwinds from hardware mix noted but partially offset by pricing. Stock faded post-print on order deceleration (non-hyperscale +14% vs +25% prior).

bullets.title: NVDA Export Control / US-China Tech Truce Under Severe Strain Post-Huang
bullets.body: Huang's exit accelerates Congressional push for tighter chip export controls: MATCH Act, AI OVERWATCH Act, Remote Access Security Act, and Chip Security Act all gaining traction in NDAA. Commerce Dept finalizing rules blocking Chinese access to advanced AI chips in SE Asia (seven countries). Megaspeed scandal involved ~240,000 NVDA chips diverted to China via Singapore/Malaysia neoclouds. Oracle cancelled major Tencent contract under Trump pressure. Chinese firms rushed to secure overseas NVDA capacity. Risk window for US-China confrontation likely opens Jan 2027 after December NDAA.

bullets.title: Value/Defensive Rotation Intensifying — Market Leadership Shifting from Growth to Quality
bullets.body: OPCO technicals flag shift from growth/tech to value/defensive/higher-quality: Russell 1000 Value relative RSI at 66 vs 33 for Growth. OPCO removes NVDA, AMAT, KLAC, GOOG, GEV from buy list; adds RSG, FAST, DRI, COST, BRK/B, PGR, PLTR, TXN. Investors Intelligence bull/bear ratio fell to 1.5 (lowest since April 2026). SPX 200-day MA at ~7,335 (~3% below Friday close); breach would shift focus to 6,700. Credit spreads failed to confirm equity rally.

bullets.title: October CPI/PPI Hot — Core PCE Tracking 0.29-0.35%; 50bp December Hike Risk
bullets.body: October core CPI +0.30% m/m (third consecutive hot print); 59% of core CPI components rising >3% m/m annualized. PPI headline 6.5% y/y cycle high; core PPI 5.0%. Core PCE tracking lowered 4bp to 0.29% post-PPI (MS: 0.35%). Governor Waller said third straight 0.3% core print would put 50bp December hike on table; Dallas Fed Logan called for at least two more hikes. Fed pricing implies ~3.5 hikes by September 2027. The CPI data is viewed as backward-looking by some analysts who expect oil decline and goods disinflation to soften future prints.

bullets.title: Data Center Capex Boom Peaks 2028/2029; Taiwan Tech Export Growth Topping
bullets.body: Multiple strategists (PSC, Piper) flag data center construction boom topping out 2028/2029 after healthy 2027: planned data center construction down 20%, Mag-8/Neoclouds slowing capex in 2028. Data center announcements/plans down sharply, threatening construction activity and tech equipment demand. Taiwan's tech export growth very likely peaking in 2026; TSMC monthly revenues, Taiwan export orders, and manufacturing PMI are leading indicators to watch. Factory construction expected to start rebounding in 2027.

bullets.title: Existing Home Sales Collapse to 2010 Lows; Housing Needs Rate Vol Relief
bullets.body: October existing home sales fell 5.5% m/m to 3.75M (SAAR) — lowest since 2010 aside from COVID lows; below both pre-COVID levels and population-adjusted norms. Single-family annualized sales at 3.4M, 27% below population-adjusted rate. Mortgage rates at highest since 2000. Median home price up only 0.4% y/y, smallest gain since February. Housing recovery requires both lower Treasury yields AND lower rate volatility — not achievable near-term in current Fed path.

bullets.title: Macro Systematic Strategies Have ~$20B US Equity Supply Remaining; CTAs Flipped Net Short
bullets.body: JPM estimates macro systematic strategies have ~$20B US equity supply remaining next week; CTAs flipped from +150% to -5% global equity exposure in October. Levered ETF sales of ~$95B over two days dropped exposure below January 2026 levels. AAII bears at 96th percentile. However, global HF gross leverage fell to 26th percentile and net leverage to 1st percentile — de-grossing largely complete. Retail flows remain bullish with strong equity and leveraged ETF buying; tech ETFs saw inflows. ~$60B potential equity demand over next month if realized vol falls to 15%.

bullets.title: Brent Crude Down 20%+ from Peak on Iran De-escalation; Physical Market in Surplus
bullets.body: Brent crude fell from $118/bbl to ~$96/bbl (IEA: oil market back in surplus in October) on de-escalated Middle East tensions and Trump signaling limited need for further Iran strikes. Oil down 4%+ on the day of de-escalation news. Lower oil removes one inflation tail risk and supports non-US equity outperformance per Jefferies. Persian Gulf refined product loadings rising to ~3M bpd; Saudi crude exports at pre-war levels for first time.

bullets.title: HUBS CEO Halligan Returns — Co-Founder 'Re-founding' Around AI
bullets.body: HubSpot co-founder Brian Halligan returned as CEO (effective Nov 12), replacing Yamini Rangan amid partner feedback of internal exhaustion and over-focus on margin optimization. CFO Kate Bueker retiring Feb 2027; Adobe's Karen Burgess joining as CFO. Company reaffirmed Q4/FY26 guidance. Analyst reactions mixed: JPM views as positive for navigation of AI monetization; KeyBanc expects aggressive restructuring and M&A acceleration; Wolfe waits for inflection in agent usage before turning constructive.

bullets.title: AMAT Beats/Raises — 2027 WFE Growth >30%; Cleanroom Availability Key Constraint
bullets.body: Applied Materials Q4 EPS $4.16 beat consensus by 2.5%; Q1 guidance of $11.10B (+2.3% above consensus). Management expects 2027 WFE to grow >30% with AMAT positioned to outperform the market; Advanced Packaging grew +90% y/y driven by HBM demand. Largest customer now providing rolling 8-quarter forecasts with no order pushouts. Cleanroom availability is primary gating factor limiting near-term upside. Sell-side 88% buy; Citi cuts PT to $580 on lower peer multiples.

bullets.title: SPX Forward P/E De-Rated from 23.2x to 18.2x; JPM Maintains 8,000 YE26 Target
bullets.body: S&P 500 forward P/E de-rated from 23.2x to 18.2x on the week — a ~4-turn compression driven by AI deleveraging and rate repricing. JPM reiterates YE26 SPX target of 8,000 (8.4% upside) with $365 EPS at 21.9x; sees pullback as positioning reset that should support AI supercycle durability. Every $100B increase in AI capex translates to ~$9 for S&P EPS (~2.5% earnings growth) in 2027. Tech forward P/E fell to 17.3x vs. 25-year avg of 20.0x.

bullets.title: Global Rate Hike Cycle Broadening — JPM Calls End of 'Immaculate Disinflation'
bullets.body: JPM's Global Data Watch warns end of 'magical thinking' on growth-without-inflation narrative. Global core inflation rebounded to 3.4% annualized through October. Fed divergence expected from other DMs: Fed hiking while BoE faces December close call, ECB keeping hikes on table. India RBI forecast to raise 25bp at next three meetings; UK BoE expected to hike in December. Japan BoJ continuing gradual increases toward neutral. Russia, Romania, Peru also tightening. The 'immaculate disinflation' dogma being formally abandoned.

bullets.title: FOXA Top Pick at Morgan Stanley After Roku Deal Closes Early; $90 PT, 37% Upside
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley resumed FOXA at Overweight and elevated to Top Pick following early close of $22B Roku acquisition. Pro forma revenue growth lifts to ~6% from low-single digits; EBITDA CAGR rises from ~1% to ~9% through CY27-30E; FCF/share compounds at ~20% through FY30. $400M+ cost synergies modeled; $500M-$1B revenue synergy excluded from base case. Fox/Tubi/Roku Channel combined hold 10%+ monthly US TV viewing, rivaling Disney and ahead of Netflix. 4:1 bull/bear skew at $100/$60.
